summary: Destroys a linked list whose owner object also optionally owns a Windows handle. First, if the byte flag at this+0x18 is non-zero, CloseHandle is invoked on the handle at this+0x10 and the handle field is zeroed when the close succeeds. The linked list rooted at this+0x0 is then walked: for each node, if the node's byte flag at node+0x8 is non-zero and the node's data pointer at node+0x0 is non-null, the data object's first vtable entry (a __thiscall release/delete method) is invoked on the data with argument 1. Every node wrapper is freed via FreeWrapper_7bcf. Finally the head, tail, cursor and count fields (this+0x0, this+0x4, this+0x8, this+0xC) are zeroed.

operations.description: The handle close path runs only when the byte flag at this+0x18 is non-zero.
CloseHandle is called on the handle value at this+0x10.
When CloseHandle returns success, the handle field at this+0x10 is zeroed.
Walks the singly linked list starting from the head pointer at this+0x0; each node's next pointer lives at node+0x4 and the walk continues while a next node exists.
For each node the destructor dispatch runs only when the node's byte flag at node+0x8 is non-zero and the node's data pointer at node+0x0 is non-null.
The data object's first vtable entry (a __thiscall method) is invoked on the data pointer with argument 1, releasing/deleting the data when the node requires it.
FreeWrapper_7bcf frees the node wrapper itself.
The list head at this+0x0 is zeroed after the list is freed.
The list tail at this+0x4 is zeroed after the list is freed.
The cursor/iterator field at this+0x8 is zeroed after the list is freed.
The element count at this+0xC is zeroed after the list is freed.
The function returns void after the list structure fields are reset.
